clue.text: Rector squared the circle?

indicators.note: squared in the sense of put straight or sorted out, so the letters of circle are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A clergyman is credited with solving the ancient geometrical puzzle of squaring the circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squared' signals an anagram: the letters of CIRCLE are reshuffled. 'The circle' looks like the impossible geometry problem, but it is only the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A rector is a parish priest, one kind of clergyman.

clue.text: Sweat — ie, invents work offering more jobs

parts.note: to sweat is to toil, and toil is labour

indicators.note: work as a verb, so the letters of ie and invents are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sweats over inventing things in a way that creates lots of employment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' is the anagram signal: IE plus INVENTS rearranged give INTENSIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A labour-intensive industry needs many workers, so it provides plenty of employment.

clue.text: Noisy reveller for whom dawn herald gets one for nothing

indicators.note: one is the letter I and nothing is the letter O, so the bird swaps an O out for an I

parts.note: the cockerel crows at dawn, so it heralds the day

explanation.surface: A rowdy partygoer is compared to a cockerel that gets something for free.
explanation.walkthrough: Change one O in ROOSTER to I. A roister, or roisterer, is someone who revels noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to make merry boisterously, and the old noun names such a rowdy merrymaker.

clue.text: Reduce council item employees carry to look indispensable

definitions.text: item employees carry to look indispensable

parts.note: to clip is to cut down or shorten
a board is a governing body or council

explanation.surface: Office workers carry a council item around so they look too important to dismiss.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a joke about office life: walking about holding a writing board makes anyone look busy.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrying a board with papers clipped to it is the classic way of looking busy and essential at work.

clue.text: Coastal resort wherein time may be put by

indicators.note: wherein means inside which, so the time letter goes into the resort word

parts.note: a seaside is a holiday place on the coast

explanation.surface: A holiday town by the sea where people may save up time for themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: To set aside money or time is to reserve it, which is what putting something by means.

clue.text: Illumination from paper could be unhealthy

definitions.text: Illumination from paper could be unhealthy

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
a lamp is a source of illumination

explanation.surface: Light given off by a newspaper might be bad for your health.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid. 'From' says the light comes after the paper, and the whole clue doubles as a warning: too much tanning can harm the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tanning device giving out ultraviolet light, overuse of which is a health risk.

clue.text: Course of time with torture

parts.note: the rack was a device for torture by stretching

explanation.surface: A process going on for some time, accompanied by torture.
explanation.definitionFit: A track is a path or racecourse, so it is a course in the sense of a route.

clue.text: Live in lustre at the boozer

indicators.note: in places the living word inside the shine word

parts.note: sheen is a soft lustre or shine
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: Someone lives in a glittering style down at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A shebeen is an unlicensed drinking den, a word from Ireland and Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Boozer is British slang for a pub, and a shebeen is an illicit bar.

clue.text: One who counts on his fingers?

definitions.text: One who counts on his fingers?

parts.words: One who counts on his fingers?
parts.note: digits are fingers, so a calculating machine working with digits is jokingly pictured as a finger-counter

explanation.surface: A slow arithmetician counts on their fingers.
explanation.walkthrough: The pun is on digit, meaning both a finger and a numeral; the machine computes with digits.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer working with discrete digits, numbers in binary, rather than continuous quantities.

clue.text: Died with violin play and forgetfulness

parts.note: OB is short for Latin obiit, he or she died, seen on gravestones

indicators.note: play as in loose movement, so the letters of violin are moved about

explanation.surface: Someone died, the violin played, and all was forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like playing the instrument, but it signals an anagram of VIOLIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblivion is the state of being forgotten or of forgetting everything.

clue.text: Get one's own back from, say, Russian flower

indicators.note: from is read as taking these pieces from the end backwards, the reading direction also hinted at by back in the definition

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means here
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Neva flows through St Petersburg

explanation.surface: Someone takes revenge using a Russian flower.
explanation.walkthrough: EG plus NEVA read backwards gives the answer. The fifteensquared blogger notes 'back' does double duty, giving the reversal as well as finishing the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To avenge a wrong is to take revenge for it, getting even with the wrongdoer.

clue.text: Leave that's fairly short

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the last letter of the word for fairly is dropped

parts.note: quite means fairly, as in quite good

explanation.surface: A remark about leave that lasts only a fairly short time.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit is to depart from a place, the same as leaving it.

clue.text: Absence of French in English city outbreak

indicators.note: in puts the absence word and the French word inside the city name

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, England
a lack is an absence of something
de is French for of

explanation.surface: Something French is missing from an English city during an epidemic.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is a Somerset city famous for its Roman baths; 'absence' as a noun is the lack, not a missing letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Black Death was the great bubonic plague outbreak of the fourteenth century.

clue.text: Range said to be a sailing blunder

indicators.note: said to be signals that the answer is how the phrase sounds when spoken

parts.note: a mistake made at sea, put as sea error

explanation.surface: A mountain range is supposedly a mistake made while sailing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a jagged chain of mountains, the Spanish word for saw.

clue.text: Shelter in former educational establishment with power

indicators.note: in places the shelter word inside the old college word

parts.note: a poly was a polytechnic, a type of British college merged into the universities in 1992
a tent is a canvas shelter

explanation.surface: A shelter in a former college has electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: British polytechnics became universities in 1992, hence 'former'.
explanation.definitionFit: Potently means powerfully, so acting with power.

clue.text: Fetish to ring in place of worship

indicators.note: in places the ring letter inside the place of worship

parts.note: a temple is a building for worship
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: Someone telephones in to a temple about a sacred object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like telephoning but is the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved post of totems, objects revered as emblems of a clan, as a fetish is revered.

clue.text: Fiddle somehow led to stand with legs apart

parts.note: a Strad is a Stradivarius violin, and a violin is a fiddle

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of led are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: A violin somehow led someone to stand with their legs spread.
explanation.definitionFit: To straddle something is to stand or sit astride it, legs on either side.

clue.text: One without faith somehow hates it

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of hates it are arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Someone without religion somehow hates it.
explanation.definitionFit: An atheist does not believe in any god, so has no religious faith.

clue.text: Pattern formerly sufficient

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
ample means enough or sufficient

explanation.surface: A design that used to be adequate.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is a model to be copied, which is what a pattern is.

clue.text: Get excited? No!

parts.note: turning the word on round gives no, the word printed in the clue

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to get excited and is told no.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as an instruction, turns ON into NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Being turned on is colloquial for becoming aroused or excited.

clue.text: Turned last of 15 round gallery

indicators.note: round says the first piece goes around the gallery name

parts.note: the last word of the answer to 15 down is pole, and a pole is a rod, an old unit of length
the Tate is the famous art gallery in London

explanation.surface: The end of a carved post is spun around a gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross-reference: the last word of 15 down is pole, and pole, rod and perch are all the same old length unit. The fifteensquared blogger disliked the device.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotated means spun or revolved, so turned round.

clue.text: One doesn't much care to be without it

definitions.text: One doesn't much care to be without it

parts.words: One doesn't much care to be without it
parts.note: someone who does not much care about anything is lacking keenness or zeal

explanation.surface: Something one would rather not do without.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests something one would hate to lose; the real reading is that apathy means lacking it.
explanation.definitionFit: Keenness or eager interest, which an indifferent person lacks.

clue.text: Drinkers find some taste in a glass or mug

indicators.note: some means a part of the phrase, so the answer sits inside taste in

explanation.surface: Drinkers find a bit of taste in their glass or tankard.
explanation.definitionFit: A stein is a large earthenware beer mug, from German.

clue.text: High note needs drink

parts.note: top means highest
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A high musical note calls for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: To tope is an old word for drinking heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Tope is a verb meaning to drink alcohol, especially to excess.

clue.text: Figure is about 80 chains

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the letters of is are read backwards

parts.note: a chain is 22 yards, and 80 of them make 1,760 yards, a mile

explanation.surface: A number is about eighty chains long.
explanation.definitionFit: A simile is a figure of speech comparing one thing to another.

clue.text: Gland inclined to Erastianism?

parts.note: Erastianism is the doctrine that the state should rule the church, so a supporter is in favour of the state

explanation.surface: A gland is accused of holding a view on church and state.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer: pro- means in favour of, and Erastians favour the state over the church.
explanation.definitionFit: The male gland around the urethra below the bladder.

clue.text: Bird that concludes with a period

definitions.meaning: bird, from rhyming slang bird-lime for time, is a prison term
a grammatical unit ending with a full stop, which Americans call a period

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' is British slang for time in prison; 'period' is the American word for a full stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a jail term handed down by a judge and a grammatical string of words ending in a full stop.

clue.text: Last under English system

indicators.note: system as in systematically rearranged, so the letters of under are put in order anew

explanation.surface: The final item sits under the English system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under' looks like a position word, but it is the fodder for the anagram signalled by 'system'.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to go on or survive, which is what enduring means.
